'''Johanna G. Nešlehová''' (born July 26, 1977){{r|cv}} is a Czech [[Mathematical statistics|mathematical statistician]] who works in Canada at [[McGill University]] as a professor in the department of mathematics and statistics.{{r|home}} Her research interests include [[Copula (probability theory)|copulas]], [[extreme value theory]], [[multivariate statistics]], and [[operational risk]].{{r|home|crmssc}}

==Education and career==
Nešlehová is originally from [[Prague]], the daughter of painter [[Pavel Nešleha]] and art historian {{ill|Mahulena Nešlehová|cs}}.{{r|crmssc}} She studied at the [[Charles University]], the [[University of Hamburg]], and the [[University of Oldenburg]], earning a degree (vordiplom) from [[University of Hamburg]] in 1999, a master's degree (diplom) from the [[University of Hamburg]] in 2000, and a doctorate from the [[University of Oldenburg]] in 2004.{{r|home}} Her dissertation, ''Dependence of Non-continuous Random Variables'', was supervised by {{ill|Dietmar Pfeifer|de|Dietmar Pfeifer (Mathematiker)}}.{{r|mg}}

After working as a postdoctoral researcher and Heinz Hopf Lecturer at [[ETH Zürich]], she joined the McGill University faculty in 2009.{{r|crmssc}} Since October 2022 she is also a professor at WU [[Vienna University of Economics and Business]].{{r|wu}}

==Book==
With Erhard Cramer, Nešlehová is the author of a German-language undergraduate textbook in introductory mathematics, ''Vorkurs Mathematik: Arbeitsbuch zum Studienbeginn in Bachelor-Studiengängen'' (Springer, 2005; 7th ed., 2018).{{r|crmssc|vm}}

==Recognition==
Nešlehová was named as an Elected Member of the [[International Statistical Institute]] in 2011.{{r|home}} In 2020 she was named a Fellow of the [[Institute of Mathematical Statistics]].{{r|home|ims}}

She was the 2019 winner of the CRM-SSC Prize in Statistics "for fundamental contributions to multivariate statistics, and in particular stochastic dependence modeling and extreme-value theory, and for her efforts to promote the sound application of statistics in risk management".{{r|crmssc}}

In 2023, Nešlehová was the second statistician (after [[Nancy Reid]] in 1995) to receive the [[Krieger–Nelson Prize]] of the [[Canadian Mathematical Society]].{{r|home|cms}}

==Personal life==
Nešlehová is married to statistician [[Christian Genest]].{{r|cv}} Their son Richard Genest was born in 2014. Johanna became a Canadian citizen in 2015.
